business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Pet Supplies and Pet Care Devices

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EFTA Convention of 4 January 1960, as amended
Agreement on Free Trade between Switzerland and the EEC of 22 July 1972
Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty of 12 November 1986, as amended by the 2009 Protocol
Convention between Switzerland and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of 2 October 1996, as amended by the 2009 and 2019 Protocols
Convention between Switzerland and the Federal Republic of Germany for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of 11 August 1971, as amended
Convention between Switzerland and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of 8 December 1977, as amended

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 621, 626-629, 632, 643, 716a-b; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (ANAG/HReg-PV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the seat canton under the supervisory authority of the Federal Office of the Commercial Register (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EAR); operational supervision by the cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung) including the Articles of Association (Statuten), filed electronically by the notary with the Cantonal Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value per share, but not less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate, must be paid up in cash (Art. 632 OR); cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) opened in the name of the company in formation at a Swiss bank and remain blocked until legal personality is acquired by entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company, following its entry in the Commercial Register, hereby (1) ratifies and confirms the subscription of the full share capital and the capital payment made in accordance with the notarized Deed of Incorporation; (2) adopts the registered office at the address in the Articles of Association; (3) appoints [Name] as Chairperson of the Board, [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Managing Officer, with individual or collective signing rights as recorded; (4) authorizes the officers to complete the SHAB publication, VAT, social insurance, and cantonal tax registrations; (5) resolves to open bank accounts and release the escrowed paid-up capital; and (6) grants the appointed officers full power to execute all related filings and banking instructions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton-registered Notary Public (öffentlicher Notar) and a Swiss bank or finance institution licensed by FINMA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Association and Deed of Incorporation before the notary; open a blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company in formation; transfer a minimum of CHF 50,000 of the nominal share capital; obtain the bank's written confirmation of the blocked deposit; the notary issues the notarial deed and capital payment statement.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association with registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, and share categories
Identification documents (passport or national ID) of founders, board members, and authorized signatories
Bank confirmation of the blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto)
Declaration of cash contribution and list of share subscriptions
Completed notarial public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank resists the blocking wording or account naming, obtain a revised confirmation or transfer the deposit to another Swiss bank; if the notary identifies statutory omissions, execute a supplementary notarial instrument correcting the Articles of Association before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via certified electronic filing by the notary; federal review by the EAR in supervisory capacity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the incorporation application, deed, statutes, shareholder list, and capital confirmation electronically; the registry examines name admissibility, seat, corporate purpose, capital, and governance provisions; upon approval, the Company acquires legal personality and receives the Swiss Business Identifier (UID).
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Minutes of the founders' general meeting
List of shareholders with subscribed and paid-up amounts
Bank blocked-capital confirmation and proof of payment
Board members' acceptance declarations and specimen signatures
Power of attorney authorizing the notary to file (per HRegV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, the notary submits a corrective declaration within the prescribed examination period; a name conflict requires amendment of the Articles of Association by notarial act; registry decisions are appealable to the cantonal supervisory authority and thereafter to the Cantonal Court under Art. 943 OR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB Publication and Organization Dossier Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) and the Cantonal Commercial Register for official records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, the registry arranges the SHAB publication within thirty days; the Company verifies published data and obtains certified commercial register excerpts for banking, tax, and payment-provider onboarding.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt (certified)
UID confirmation issued by the registry
Final Articles of Association and board organization chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, submit a written expedition or correction request to the registry; the registry orders the SHAB corrigendum at no cost to the Company; no impact on legal personality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Insurance and Accident Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV – MWST division), cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse), and SUVA for mandatory accident insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with ESTV for VAT, either mandatorily if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 annually or voluntarily to recover input VAT on logistics and payment-provider fees; register as an employer with the Compensation Office for AHV/IV/EO contributions and with SUVA for occupational accident insurance effective from the first hire; file the relevant registration forms and retain confirmations in the corporate compliance file.
required_dossiers: UID confirmation and certified commercial register excerpt
Bank details of the Company's operating account
Employer registration data for AHV/IV/EO (salary records)
Declaration of expected turnover for VAT threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is filed after the threshold is already exceeded, submit a self-denunciation with justification to ESTV to obtain penalty relief under Art. 210 VATA; if the Compensation Office queries employer data, provide corrected payroll declarations promptly; late registrations may be regularized without sanction in minor negligent cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal Tax Registration and Payment-Rails KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the seat canton and the payment-service providers Stripe and PayPal subject to FINMA anti-money-laundering supervision.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete cantonal corporate income tax and capital tax registration; submit final Articles of Association and board appointments; onboard Stripe and PayPal using the UID, certified domicile proof, entity governance documents, and beneficial ownership declarations; complete the standard low-risk AML KYC for e-commerce pet supplies merchant accounts.
required_dossiers: Certified commercial register excerpt with UID
Notarized Articles of Association and board appointment minutes
Beneficial ownership declaration (Swiss Form A/B)
Operational bank account details
E-commerce privacy policy and returns/refund policy for merchant underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a payment provider requests enhanced KYC, provide an apostilled excerpt and certified statutes; if the cantonal tax office requires supplemental schedules, respond within the stated deadline; tax orders are appealable under cantonal tax procedure, and payment-provider decisions may be cured by submitting the dormant-company explanation and projected sales evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 electronic retailing of pet supplies; if physical warehousing or pick-and-pack premises are deployed, the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate (Kantonales Arbeitsinspektorat), the municipal building authority (Bauamt), and the cantonal fire inspectorate become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating license required for pure e-commerce retailing; a municipal business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) will suffice for any warehouse or office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) and the competent cantonal environmental department of the seat canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – electronic retailing is not listed in Annex 1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV); no EIA screening, scoping, or formal report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC-emission thresholds apply; general obligations under the Federal Act on the Protection of the Environment (USG) require packaging-waste minimization, separate collection of cardboard and plastic wrappings, and, where applicable, advance recycling contributions for beverage containers and batteries; if warehousing is added, the Ordinance on the Avoidance and Disposal of Waste (VVEA) governs collection, recycling, and disposal tracking.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense or structural clearance is required for a pure e-commerce head office; for leased office or warehouse space, the Company must obtain fire safety certification from the cantonal fire inspectorate, structural load approval for racked storage, and occupational-safety confirmation covering lighting, ventilation, sanitation, and emergency exits under the Swiss Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz) and SUVA accident-prevention regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), Effingerstrasse 20, 3003 Bern, Switzerland; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and UID management via the ESTV eServices portal; cantonal corporate income tax administered by the cantonal tax administration of the registered office (e.g., Zug or Zürich).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned AG established in Switzerland: (i) incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft and register it in the commercial register (Handelsregister) of the canton of registered office; (ii) the Swiss Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the business identification number (UID, format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX), which serves as the unified statutory TIN for tax, VAT, customs and statistics; (iii) file the VAT registration with the ESTV (form 744e for foreign-controlled entities; online via the ESTV ePortal) once annual net taxable turnover from Swiss supplies exceeds CHF 100,000; the application must include the notarized articles of incorporation, commercial register extract, certificate of capital paid in (minimum CHF 100,000, at least CHF 50,000 paid up), shareholding structure, proof of registered office and place of effective management, and, where no Swiss residence is maintained, designation of a Swiss tax representative (Art. 67 MWSTG); (iv) for foreign distance sellers of pet supplies into Switzerland without a Swiss registered office, the simplified ESTV distance-selling registration procedure applies once Swiss distance-sales turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, with the same UID/VAT number being used for customs clearance and electronic reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Swiss AG is a separate resident tax subject under Art. 58 ff. of the Federal Tax Harmonization Act; no pass-through treatment is available to an AG; corporate income tax is imposed at federal (effective ~8.5% incl. surcharge), cantonal, and communal levels with combined effective rates of approximately 11.9% in Zug and 19.7% in Zürich; residence is established by statutory seat or place of effective management; worldwide income is taxable with territorial carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments and Swiss real estate; for VAT, CH_AG is a taxable person (Art. 10 MWSTG) upon exceeding the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold; Switzerland has no tax-exempt zone applicable to e-commerce entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid mismatch election. Applicable statutory elections for a CH_AG engaged in pet-supplies e-commerce: (i) VAT group registration (Art. 21(2) MWSTG) permitting related Swiss undertakings to be treated as one taxable person; (ii) net tax rate / Saldo method election (Art. 36a and 37 MWSTG) available to taxpayers with annual taxable turnover not exceeding CHF 5 million, applying a sectoral flat VAT rate (for retail trade of goods, currently 2.6% of turnover) in lieu of input VAT deduction; (iii) participation exemption (Art. 69 DBG and cantonal statutes) applicable to qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (10% substantial participation), applied as a statutory deduction; (iv) voluntary VAT registration from the first franc of turnover, and (v) election of the business fiscal year (calendar or 12-month period) as VAT settlement period.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT); Swiss VAT (Mehrwertsteuer/MWST, Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée/TVA, Imposta sul valore aggiunto/IVA) levied under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (SR 641.20) and administered by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual net taxable turnover (excluding VAT) on Swiss supplies for Swiss-resident businesses (Art. 10(2)(a) MWSTG); for foreign distance sellers of goods into Switzerland (including e-commerce of pet supplies), a CHF 100,000 Swiss distance-sales turnover threshold applies (Art. 10(2)(b) MWSTG); voluntary registration is available from the first franc; marketplace platform operators may be deemed the supplier where the underlying foreign merchant has no Swiss UID and the platform controls the delivery or invoicing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance API, mandatory continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime applies in Switzerland. Electronic invoices in PDF, XML, EDI, or other system-readable formats are recognized under Art. 26 MWSTG provided the statutory invoice content is present (name and address of supplier and recipient, date, type and quantity of goods, consideration, tax rate or VAT exemption notice). The Swiss market standard is the SIX eBill framework and the QR-bill payment slip, which is mandatory for paper payment invoices since 1 January 2021; the QR-bill replaces the traditional ISR payment slip and must contain the IBAN and QR code. B2G e-invoicing via the eBill platform is increasingly required by Swiss cantons and communes for public procurement but is not yet a universal federal mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Switzerland to a foreign country are zero-rated under Art. 23(2)(1) MWSTG, provided the exporter proves by customs and transport documentation that the goods left Swiss territory and the consignee is located abroad. For the ISIC 4791 pet-supplies e-commerce model, the 0% rate applies to sales where CH_AG ships goods via postal or courier services to foreign customers, subject to the export proof bundle described below. Services related to export or foreign movable goods, such as storage, handling, and transport, may qualify for the 0% rate under Art. 23(1) MWSTG. Off-store border trade, deliveries to Swiss customs warehouses without onward export, and intragroup consignments of Swiss stock do not qualify. Swiss VAT law does not stipulate a fixed statutory FX repatriation deadline for zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is used as the internal best-evidence period for completed export consideration and for retaining export documentation, consistent with accounting international practice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration: electronic TARES/e-dec declaration number and the Swiss Customs export accompanying document (Ausfuhrbegleitdokument / export confirmation) proving that the goods crossed the Swiss border

Transport document proving physical export: bill of lading (B/L), CMR waybill, air waybill, courier manifest, postal dispatch certificate, or multimodal transport document showing dispatch from Switzerland to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice / VAT zero-rated invoice issued by CH_AG stating the exported pet supplies, quantity, customs value, Incoterms, destination country, and recipient details
Inward Remittance Certificate or banking evidence of foreign-currency payment for the exported goods, supporting the consideration and exchange-rate treatment
Proof of receipt abroad, such as a signed delivery note, consignee confirmation, or courier track-and-trace record evidencing final delivery to the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV treats zero-rating claims as high-risk and audits e-commerce exporters intensively. If the export documentation bundle is missing, incomplete, or internally inconsistent, the 0% rate is retrospectively denied, VAT is reassessed at the 8.1% standard rate, input VAT deductions are clawed back with default interest, and the exporter is exposed to evasion penalties. Intentional or attempted tax evasion triggers administrative fines of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 57 VStrR) and criminal monetary or custodial sanctions; the limitation period extends to ten years, or fifteen years in case of intentional evasion. False distance-selling filings and incorrect customs declarations may simultaneously be sanctioned by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (Oberzolldirektion) under the Customs Penal Act, with additional penalties and publication of final decisions in severe cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) with regulatory oversight from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking conduct; the Swiss State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) handles cross-border financial market policy. Switzerland maintains no exchange-control authority or approval mechanism for routine commercial payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates as a fully liberalised capital and current account economy; CHF is freely convertible and export/import payments face no conversion licensing, retrenchment restrictions, or profit-remittance ceilings. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are legally unrestricted; only the 35% Swiss withholding tax applies and may be reduced or reclaimed under the relevant double-taxation agreement. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft can therefore hold and remit worldwide proceeds without central-bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion deadlines, and no quota obligations. Export receipts from electronic pet-supplies retail may remain in the original currency, be retained in foreign bank accounts, or be converted into CHF at free-market rates. Swiss banks only report cross-border payment flows to the SNB for statistical balance-of-payments purposes, and no repatriation or conversion ratio is ever triggered.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) in CHF with multi-currency overlay
Operational Account / Receivables Account in CHF and EUR
E-commerce Payment Account / Operational Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility for an offshore electronic-money institution (EMI). A FINMA-licensed Swiss bank must remain the master treasury bank for statutory capital escrow, SIC clearing, and regulatory reporting. A UK/EU EMI can support low-value Stripe/PayPal collections and supplier payouts, but it is not a permissible venue for share capital deposits or principal liquidity management under Swiss corporate and AML law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The AMLA and FINMA Circular 2023/01 require identity and beneficial-ownership verification for all mandate holders. Physical presentation of original passports or certified copies before a bank officer, notary, or Swiss consular official is ordinarily required for the managing director and each signatory. Remote videographic identification is accepted by some banks for low-risk e-commerce clients if combined with a notarised ID copy, apostilled corporate documents, and a Swiss registered office; a practical recommendation is to hold one in-person director sign-off in Switzerland to avoid account-opening friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder residing in a high-risk jurisdiction or reliance on crypto-derived capital funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised and apostilled constitutional documents, a source-of-wealth declaration for each shareholder, a board resolution identifying all beneficial owners, a certified fiat audit trail with transaction reference numbers, and a FINMA-/OSA-compliant AML opinion, including a bank reference from the shareholder's home institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contribution distributed by a nondescript third-party remitter rather than the registered shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the signed capital-payment instruction, underlying share-subscription agreement, bank certificate of receipt (Sperrkonto), and an affidavit of causal connection; use a single bank-to-bank credit routing that matches the shareholder register exactly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border merchant transactions with Stripe/PayPal creating unexplained debit-credit cycles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the entity's internal AML risk file, customer and merchant-flow reports, payment-volume projections, settlement reports, contract index proving underlying sales of ISIC 4791 pet products, and a group officer compliance attestation that no unlicensed money-services activity is being performed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid international payment velocity inconsistent with the declared e-commerce treasury function
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a cashflow model showing cash-conversion-cycle consistency, supplier invoice ledger, logistics/packaging bills, and the PSP settlement schedule; implement monthly reconciliation statements to demonstrate that every debit or credit reflects requested treasury activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must arrive via SWIFT MT103/RUR or a fiscally transparent SEPA transfer to a Swiss blocked account in the name of the Aktiengesellschaft, with a clear purpose code under Swiss balance-of-payments surveys (direct investment / equity capital). The payment reference should state 'Kapitalerhöhung' or 'capital contribution'; the remitter must appear in the commercial register and beneficial-ownership mapping. For statutory validation, the bank issues a capital-escrow confirmation enabling notarial verification; after registration, the funds are released into the operational treasury account. There is no FX surrender or central-bank approval step, but the incoming amount should correspond to the stated share capital in CHF.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic and international disbursements use SIC for CHF, euroSIC/SEPA for euros, and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border non-SEPA payments. Trade financed imports of pet products can be executed via documentary letters of credit issued as SWIFT MT700/MT710 to the exporter's bank. The treasury accepts Stripe and PayPal as purely ancillary clearing rails that settle to a dedicated Swiss collecting account; direct supplier payments must never transit the PSP. Bulk multi-currency payroll and procurement payments use the bank's corporate electronic banking portal, with MT940/MT950 statements supplying daily liquidity reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CHF FX forwards (plain vanilla, bank-quoted)
FX swaps between CHF, USD, EUR, GBP and CNY
Cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet interest-rate and currency matching
Plain-vanilla FX call or put options with cash settlement or physical delivery
FX collars and zero-cost structures using forward and option combinations
Exchange-traded currency futures through regulated infrastructures, to the extent compatible with FINMA margining rules
Non-deliverable forwards only for exotic and illiquid emerging-market currencies in which Swiss banks are prepared to quote; CHF and G10 currencies are fully deliverable, rendering NDFs unnecessary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) comprising balance sheet, income statement and notes, adopted by the shareholders at the Annual General Meeting together with the report of the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing is required for a small AG; signed copies are archived at the registered office and must be made available on demand to the Commercial Register Office, tax authorities and the statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting within six months of the financial year-end (Art. 699 para. 3 CO); for a calendar-year company by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM and adopt the annual accounts exposes directors to administrative fines up to CHF 5,000, personal liability for damages and, after formal notice, compulsory dissolution ordered by the commercial register authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Signed annual financial statements, Board report and mandatory auditor's report lodged with the commercial register (filing duty triggered by ordinary audit obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the balance sheet date; for a calendar-year entity by December 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial register fine under the register enforcement regime; after two formal reminders the register authority may strike the AG off the register and open compulsory liquidation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return (Umsatzsteuererklärung / déclaration TVA) reporting taxable supplies of pet products sold through the e-commerce payment rails (Stripe, PayPal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar-year taxation period if an annual filing basis has been granted; ordinarily March 1 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, administrative fines up to CHF 8,000 for minor infringements and up to 30% of the evaded tax for wilful evasion; the ESTV may additionally estimate the taxable basis

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required when the AG exceeds at least two of the three following criteria in each of two consecutive business years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, sales revenue above CHF 40 million, annual average of more than 250 full-time employees; listed public companies and companies with superior public interest are also subject to ordinary audit. AGs below these thresholds must undergo a limited audit unless they employ on an annual average 10 full-time employees or fewer and all shareholders unanimously waive any audit (limited-audit opt-out)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss statutory accounting under Arts. 957-963b CO (Swiss GAAP as interpreted by the Swiss Institute of Certified Accountants and Tax Experts); IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER may be adopted and are mandatory for listed companies; consolidated accounts, if required, also follow IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Board must maintain the commercial register's shareholder data and the internal economic beneficial-owner list under Art. 3a AMLA. The share register (Aktienbuch) is annotated without undue delay on every transfer of registered shares; the economic beneficial owner list must be updated immediately upon a change of ultimate control and verified by the Board at least annually. No separate public annual UBO return is filed in Switzerland, but the register and the beneficial-owner list must be produced to judicial authorities, MROS and tax prosecution offices on demand; a misleading or omitted entry is punishable by fines and imprisonment sanctions of the AML regime
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share register (Aktienbuch) listing all registered shareholders and their stakes (Art. 686 CO)
Register of economic beneficial owners under Art. 3a AMLA
Minute book of shareholder and board meetings with supporting corporate decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,150 - 5,800 (CHF 1,000 - 5,000) per year for a fiduciary registered office, correspondence handling, secretarial services and annual register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 11,500 (CHF 3,000 - 10,000) for a limited audit; USD 0 for an opted-out small company with unanimous shareholder waiver and average headcount of 10 or fewer

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax headline rate 8.5% on net after-tax profit, equal to approximately 7.83% effective on pre-tax profit. Combined federal and cantonal/municipal rates for a Zug-registered AG are approximately 14.3%–14.6%; a Zurich AG is approximately 21.1%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss law does not provide general corporate income tax holidays. Permanent effective-rate incentives for an AG include participation relief on dividends and capital gains from qualifying foreign and domestic participations (10% or more, or CHF 1 million minimum), the cantonal patent box (up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income), the R&D super deduction (up to 50% additional cantonal/municipal deduction), and loss carry-forward relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss federal/cantonal corporate income tax return designated 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' (Federal Direct Tax return for legal entities), filed electronically through the Federal Tax Administration's SwissTax system and the relevant cantonal eTax portal (e.g. eTax ZG, eTax ZH, eTax GE).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a unified return is filed once per tax period, normally on a calendar-year basis unless the company has an approved different business year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The canonical deadline is six months after the end of the business year; for a 31 December year-end this means 30 June of the following year. The cantonal tax administration may grant a written extension of up to three months, or longer in complex or audited cases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Commercial Register (HR) number, UID tax number, registered office, date of incorporation, board of directors, authorized signatories, investigation of ultimate beneficial owner, and confirmation of the company's limited liability status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) enters the Swiss PE address and Swiss-based management details. Foreign shareholders are not reported in this box unless they also have a Swiss PE or Swiss tax registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The taxable profit is reconciled from statutory financial statements: online sales revenue from Stripe/PayPal settlements, less returns and discounts, cost of goods sold for pet supplies and pet care devices, logistics and marketing expenses, personnel costs, depreciation, royalties, interest expense, and other deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a foreign shareholder sells goods through a Swiss e-commerce warehouse, employee base, or other permanent establishment, only income attributable to the Swiss PE is reportable. Cost and revenue allocation among foreign head office and Swiss PE must comply with the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with shareholders, members of the board, and foreign related entities: intercompany purchases, commission, royalty, management fee, interest-bearing loans, accounts receivable/payable, and declaration of dividends and Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders receiving dividends must provide a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership documentation to claim reduced treaty withholding. All intercompany transactions with a foreign parent or affiliate require explicit arm's length substantiation and the transfer pricing method used.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing and procedural non-compliance attracts a supervisory fine of up to CHF 10,000 under the Federal Act on Direct Tax (DBG Art. 174) and equivalent cantonal provisions. Unpaid tax bears default interest at approximately 4.5% per annum simple interest. Deliberate under-declaration or concealment triggers tax evasion penalties of 25%–150% of the evaded tax depending on negligence or intent, and criminal tax fraud prosecution with imprisonment up to three years if false or falsified documents are used. There is no fixed daily late surcharge; instead, the cantonal authority combines the procedural fine, default interest, and evasion penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed by the Swiss AG, unless the non-resident shareholder qualifies for an exemption under a double taxation agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss company must deduct and remit 35% at the source. A foreign beneficial owner then files a withholding tax refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid, using Form 82 or the FTA e-refund procedure. The application must include the foreign tax residency certificate (TRC), proof of beneficial ownership, a declaration of the shareholding percentage, and any DTA waiver. The FTA refunds the excess of 35% over the applicable treaty rate (generally 0%–15% under Swiss DTAs; often 0% or 5% for qualifying parent companies). DTA relief by way of an at-source reduction may only be granted if the specific DTA and FTA authorization permit it.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Switzerland imposes no statutory withholding tax on intellectual-property licence fees; under most Swiss DTAs royalty rates are 0% or exempt. Interest: Swiss statutory withholding tax of 35% applies to taxable interest from Swiss bonds, money-market instruments, securitized debt obligations, and certain intercompany financing instruments; ordinary non-securitized intercompany loans and bank loans are generally not within the Swiss WHT net. Treaty rates for residual interest typically range from 0% to 10%, and treaty benefits require TRC submission and beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss tax law does not impose a separate mandatory Local File/Master File filing threshold in the annual corporate return. However, Swiss tax authorities apply OECD transfer pricing guidelines and require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation upon audit once cross-border related-party transactions reach commercial significance; a de facto threshold for maintaining a local file is annual related-party turnover or charges above CHF 1,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for Swiss-headquartered groups with consolidated group revenue of CHF 900 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not have UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Nonetheless, Swiss courts and the FTA apply an abuse-of-law doctrine that requires genuine economic substance to respect the corporate form, grant DTA relief, and allow withholding tax refunds. A Swiss AG must maintain a real seat and effective management in Switzerland, have premises, a resident board or management, personnel, books, bank accounts and decision-making relevant to the online pet-supplies business. A letterbox company with no warehouse, no employees and no actual management substance is disregarded, its income reattributed to the real beneficial owner, and treaty/WHT benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally under-reporting Stripe/PayPal turnover, inflating cost of goods sold, fabricating purchase invoices, omitting Swiss e-commerce revenues, or knowingly filing a false federal/cantonal corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Federal Act on Direct Tax (Art. 174–175 and Art. 186), the taxpayer must pay the evaded tax, default interest and a procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; evasion penalties range from 25% to 150% of the evaded tax. Where forged books, false certificates, or deceptive documents are used, the offense is tax fraud, punishable by imprisonment up to three years or a criminal fine, plus confiscation of illicitly gained assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, CFOs, and anyone who signed or prepared a false return are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax and associated penalties under Swiss company law (Art. 754 CO). Criminal tax fraud can lead to personal criminal fines, travel bans, asset freezes, and exclusion from serving as a board member.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a letterbox: no physical Swiss office, no Swiss employees, no active management decisions, and using nominee directors with no real authority to route revenue and avoid substance while claiming Swiss tax residency and double-taxation treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA and cantonal tax authorities may disregard the corporate entity under the Swiss abuse-of-law doctrine, reattribute the taxable income to the actual entrepreneur or foreign beneficiary, deny treaty benefits and withholding tax refunds, impose a 35% withholding tax on deemed dividends, and assess evasion penalties. The Commercial Register can also strike off the company for lack of legal organization under Art. 731b CO.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who lend their names to a letterbox AG are personally exposed to administrative fines, civil restitution, criminal liability for false declarations, travel restrictions, and Swiss mutual legal assistance proceedings; the corporate veil can be pierced where the shell is used to commit tax fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structurally shifting Swiss e-commerce profits to an offshore related company through excessive foreign sourcing markups, non-arm's-length royalty or service fees, unjustified interest on shareholder loans, or undocumented intercompany payment flows that have no economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax administration will apply the OECD arm's length standard and adjust taxable income, disallow excessive deductions, recharacterize the excess as a constructive dividend subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax, and impose default interest plus tax evasion penalties of up to 150% of the additional assessed tax. Willful or falsified transfer pricing documentation can elevate the case to criminal tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length contracts knowing they are designed to evade Swiss tax are personally liable for the resulting tax deficit and penalties; in cross-border cases, directors may face asset freezes, mutual legal assistance, travel bans, and extradition or criminal prosecution in the foreign jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the pet-supplies online store and Stripe/PayPal payment accounts to layer or conceal criminal proceeds, processing card payments for unlicensed third parties, issuing fake refunds to move value, generating fictitious customer transactions, or failing to cooperate with Payment Service Provider KYC and AML investigations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis (money laundering) and Art. 305ter (lack of financial diligence) impose imprisonment up to three years, raised to five years in aggravated cases, and fines up to CHF 500,000. Criminal assets are subject to confiscation under Art. 70 et seq.; payment providers may terminate merchant contracts, freeze funds, and report suspicious transactions to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately ignore red flags, facilitate laundering through online payment rails, or personally benefit from disguised transactions face criminal prosecution, confiscation, civil damages to the company, professional disqualification, travel bans, and, in serious cases, extradition or mutual legal assistance.
